BMD Titanium PLIF GW Implant®. Depth (D) 24 / 28 / 33mm, height (H) 7–17mm, width (W) 10 or 12mm. Lordosis 8°, 12°, 16° & 20°. Internal & surface grid structure, 700µm pore size, reinforced edges. Implanted in pairs; oblique single-implant placement uses the largest footprint that fits the anatomy.
Device & indications. Ti-6Al-4V ELI, 3D-printed 700µm cube-lattice. For degenerative/postop lumbar disc involvement (rupture, osteochondrosis, stenosis, pseudarthrosis); traumatic disc involvement only without traumatic vertebral or posterior-column instability.
Contraindications & warnings. Infection/fever · obesity · component allergy · osteopenia/osteoporosis (relative) · anatomy unsuited to spinal implants. Size/placement accuracy is critical; posterior supplemental fixation strongly recommended; not a stand-alone load-bearing device; spine-trained surgeons only. Full adverse-effect list (migration, breakage, nerve injury, infection, non-union & more) and complete indications/warnings are in the Global Biomedica IFU — always follow the current version.
1

Preparation and Approach

  • Radiolucent table; abdomen free of pressure.
  • Confirm level on fluoroscopy, mark segment.
  • Standard incision; expose spinous process & facet joint.
  • Drill/Kerrison to resect lamina & facet as needed — avoid full facet resection.
2

Decompression and Discectomy

  • Pedicle screws + slight distraction ease discectomy.
  • Decompress foramen/canal; retract dural sac medially.
  • Window the posterolateral annulus; clear the disc.
  • Leave bony endplates intact — injury risks subsidence.
3

Distraction

Fig. 3 · Intervertebral disc space
  • Distractors 7–17mm, grooved at 24/28/33mm depth.
  • Start smallest — avoid over-distraction; turn clockwise.
  • Step up one size on the counter side for parallel distraction.
4

Determination of Implant Size

Fig. 5 · Determining the implant size
  • Trial by height, width & depth of the disc space.
  • Load trial into the Trial Holder; confirm fit on X-ray — tight & accurate.
5

Implant Insertion — Mounting

Fig. 6 · Implant mounting
  • Open the sterile implant matching the trial size.
  • Seat implant on the Inserter tips into its lateral notches.
  • Hand-tighten the screwcap to lock it before insertion.
6

Implant Insertion — Placement

Fig. 7 · Place the implant
  • Place in pairs; oblique single — use largest fitting footprint.
  • Tap in gently with the mallet.
  • First implant must not cross midline.
  • 9mm height & below — width equals or exceeds height, so the bone window can go straight in, already in line with the vertebra.
  • Above 9mm — insert sideways, then rotate into position (Step 7).
Protect neural structures throughout — nerve root retractor at all times; rough porous surface raises soft-tissue adherence risk.
7

Implant Rotation

Fig. 8 · Implant rotation
  • Hexagonal Key to reorient the implant in the disc space if needed.
Orientation check — T-handle in line with the patient (not necessarily as pictured) means the implant's bone windows are in line with the vertebra.
8

Completion of Surgery

Fig. 9 · Final position
  • Final fluoroscopic position check.
  • Posterior supplemental fixation strongly recommended.
  • Close as usual; document implants used (patient labels supplied).
  • No specific postop care — standard hospital protocol.
R

Implant Removal

Fig. 10 · Implant removal
  • Inserter or Universal Removal Instrument, clockwise onto implant threads.
  • Avoid pushing the implant posteriorly.
  • Remove bone overgrowth/osteophytes first if needed.
i
